    How we score deals

    We only link to public pages. No login walls, and no bypassing bot protection. If a price is not shown on the page, we write “on request” — even when an internal API exposes a number.

    Badges

    • Super deal at least 20% below the used median (at least 2 comparables), or at least 50% off a documented new price, or both (≥ 45% off new and ≥ 10% below the median).
    • Good deal at least 10% below the median, or at least 35% off new when there are no comparables.
    • Market price within ±10% of the median, or 20–35% off new with no comparables.
    • High at least 10% above the median, or less than 20% off new with no comparables.

    Comparables, in order, once at least two other priced listings exist: (1) same make and model; (2) same category, make and size class; (3) same category and size class. A hobby table is not compared with a production table, nor a 44-ton brake with a 200-ton brake. New in-stock machines are not used as comparables for used listings, and the reverse. Age is brought to the listing’s year with an estimated 8% declining-balance factor per year (capped at 10 years) — a CoupeFab estimate, not an appraisal. Hover or tap a badge to see the arithmetic (e.g. “42% off new, 18% below the used median”).

    A new-price figure is shown only from an official manufacturer or authorized-dealer page (URL + date), or, failing that, a clearly labelled “Estimated new price” backed by at least two dealer or press sources. We never invent that number. A used machine may include options the base price does not, or the reverse.

    A price-drop mark appears when the published figure has fallen since we first saw the listing. Days on market are counted from that first sighting. A listing missing for 14 days is marked stale; “sold” is used only when the seller says so.

    1 USD = 1.4219 CAD (November 25, 2026)

    • Hypertherm XPR300 power supply (MSRP) — Authorized-dealer published price for the XPR300 power supply only; not applied to complete tables
    • Haas VF-2 estimated new price (2 press sources) — No official haascnc.com price reachable (HTTP 403). Estimate US$70,995 from MachineTool Index + Open Factory, dated 26 Nov 2026

Buy-now of 137 500 CAD was read from this public lot page earlier on 26 Nov 2026; kept as last confirmed, not re-verified this run.
    Checklist (buying in Quebec)

    This is a shop-floor canvas, not an inspection. Always verify in person.

    • Shop envelope. Useful dimensions versus doors, crane and height; actual voltage (208 / 460 / 600 V); compressed air and dryer; dust collector or water table already in place.
    • Power source and tooling. Make, model, amperage or power, consumables, hours if given, working THC or control. An advertised “capacity” is not a production finish — ask to see your typical part cut or machined.
    • Mechanics. Backlash in racks or screws, squareness, rails, cables, rust, leaks.
    • Control and licences. Controller, backups, CAM software and licences: what is included, what must be bought again.
    • History. Retrofits (when, by whom), parts availability in Canada, original documentation.
    • Trial. See the machine run. Measure a test part. Listen for limit-switch and arc faults.
    • Logistics and contract. Sold as-is, dismantling, freight, taxes (GST/QST), availability. An “ex-works” price without a crane or a move is not a price in your yard.
